record.original_question:
Let A ∈ GL_n(R) and Γ ⊂ R^n a full rank lattice. Let ψ be an orthonormal (or Parseval) wavelet associated with (A,Γ), and let ψ̂ be its Fourier transform.

Does Calderón’s formula ∑_{j∈Z} |ψ̂((A^T)^j ξ)|^2 = 1 hold for almost every ξ ∈ R^n?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 1$, let $A \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{R})$ be an invertible real $n \times n$ matrix, and let $\Gamma \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a full-rank lattice. For $\psi \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$ define the associated wavelet system
$$\{ \psi_{j,k}(x) := |\det A|^{j/2}\, \psi(A^j x - k) : j \in \mathbb{Z},\; k \in \Gamma \}.$$
Call $\psi$ an orthonormal wavelet associated with $(A,\Gamma)$ if this system is an orthonormal basis of $L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$, and a Parseval wavelet if the system is a Parseval (normalized tight) frame for $L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$, i.e.
$$\|f\|_2^2 = \sum_{j \in \mathbb{Z}} \sum_{k \in \Gamma} |\langle f, \psi_{j,k}\rangle|^2 \quad \text{for all } f \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^n).$$
Let $\widehat{\psi}$ denote the Fourier transform of $\psi$.

Question: Does the Calderón formula
$$\sum_{j \in \mathbb{Z}} |\widehat{\psi}((A^T)^j \xi)|^2 = 1 \quad \text{for almost every } \xi \in \mathbb{R}^n$$
hold for every orthonormal wavelet (or, more generally, every Parseval wavelet) $\psi$ associated with $(A, \Gamma)$, with no further assumption on $A$ or $\Gamma$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is known to hold for special classes of dilations (expanding, expanding on a subspace, or dilations satisfying the lattice counting estimate). Recent work establishes the Calderón sum formula for orthonormal wavelet bases for arbitrary dilation and lattice pairs under a mild additional regularity condition on the wavelet, which partially resolves the conjecture but does not settle the unconditional version of the problem.

status_evidence.title: On the Calderón sum formula for wavelet systems
status_evidence.snippet: Calderón sum formula for orthonormal wavelet bases holds for arbitrary dilation and translation matrices under a mild condition on the wavelet function ... partially solves a conjecture by Bownik and Lemvig.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work partially resolves the problem under a mild condition on the wavelet.

status_evidence.title: Wavelets for Non-expanding Dilations and the Lattice Counting Estimate
status_evidence.snippet: Characterization of Parseval wavelet frames is known for dilations satisfying the lattice counting estimate.
status_evidence.claim: The Calderón formula and characterization of Parseval frames are established only for special dilation classes.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Wavelet Theory (Bownik)
status_evidence.snippet: List of open problems including Calderón sum formula for general (A, Γ).
status_evidence.claim: The general (A,Γ) version of the Calderón formula appears in lists of open wavelet problems.
